column3: Near-verbatim parallel: righteous work benefits its doer while evil returns upon the self.
Directly fixes each self to its own deeds in an exact, unjust-free settlement.
Repentance joined to righteous work supports reorientation, but lacks the self-preparation image.
Near-verbatim parallel: good and evil action return upon the actor without divine injustice.
The immediately preceding survey of earlier polytheists supplies the consequential horizon for disbelief.
Righteous deeds receive a good reward, supporting the fruitful outcome of such action.
Righteous, believing action yields a good life and fitting recompense for the doer.
Immediate continuation distinguishes faithful righteous action rewarded from disbelievers denied divine love.
Shares the mahhada preparation root and concretizes a made-ready condition.
States that disbelief returns to its bearer and that deeds are disclosed at return.
Inescapable recompense is explicitly tied to what people used to do.
Condemns the human for extreme disbelief, but does not state its personal result.
Contrasts evil's matching repayment with the abundant outcome of righteous believing action.
The irreversible day immediately before the focus frames the eventual division produced by present action.
The bad resting-place image gives a penal counterpart to preparing one's own future ground.
Near-parallel wording makes disbelief fall upon its bearer and increase loss.
Same-surah return to God supplies the destination at which present preparation is realized.
Places belief and disbelief beside accountable action seen by God.
Righteous action verifies a person's declared orientation, though it lacks the future-ground image.
Disbelief becomes settled rejection and criminality, but personal consequence is indirect.
Betrayal is described as wrongdoing against one's own self.
Thankfulness benefits the self, while disbelief leaves God independent, sharply locating consequence with the actor.
The disjoined letters do not clarify disbelief, righteous action, or personal preparation.
Names disbelievers on a hard day, with only a distant outcome parallel.
Unbelievers are gathered to a bad resting place, a relevant negative bedding image.
Same-surah challenge to associating others with God supports the disbelief side, without personal consequence.
Its rejected contrast route and focus on despair do not clarify the focus reading.
Thankfulness is explicitly for oneself, while disbelief leaves the Lord independent.
Each self argues for itself and receives full settlement for what it did.
Faith and righteous action receive a good recompense and easing treatment.
Endured deeds are written as righteous work whose reward is not lost.
The opening report of Roman defeat does not clarify the focus relation.
Forgetting God rebounds as being made to forget one's own self.
Disbelief is mentioned against divine independence, but not its effect on the disbeliever.
Same-surah creation-and-provision argument exposes association, but does not develop personal return.
Faithlessness results in deeds being nullified, a consequential but distant parallel.
Trust in God alone does not materially develop the focus's personal-result structure.
The deathbed request to return anticipates the missed chance to perform righteous work.
Faith and righteous action receive an enduring reward, but without self-directed preparation.
The earth as a prepared bed supplies the concrete metaphor behind making ready a future ground.
The forecast of Roman victory does not clarify the focus relation.
Righteous believers receive gardens as lodging, a future dwelling prepared by their response.
An intentional act has a personally tasted consequence and specified repair.
Same-surah judgment scene shows associates failing and former allegiance being disowned.
Association nullifies one's work and makes one a loser, directly showing a deed's destructive return.
Falsehood is said to fall upon its bearer, echoing personal liability.
Every self is recompensed for what it acquired, without injustice.
Only identifies disbelievers rushing toward the messenger, without relevant consequence.
The cradle term is lexical only; the verse does not develop preparation or personal return.
The reliable divine promise in the same surah underwrites the coming fulfillment, though indirectly.
Repentance, faith, and righteous work lead to entry without injustice.
Hell is named a bad resting place, the negative counterpart to a prepared dwelling.
Same-surah messengers, criminal punishment, and support for believers extend the moral division.
Faith, righteous work, truth, and patience form a sustained pattern of salvific action.
Intentional commitments entail accountability and repair, but the legal context is narrow.
Those who wronged themselves confront their denied evil deeds at death.
The communities are not wronged by God; they wrong their own selves.
Disbelief results in ruin and the loss of one's deeds.
The command to glorify at set times does not materially clarify the focus relation.
After mercy, disbelief and presumptuous claims lead to disclosure of deeds and severe punishment.
The request to return and do righteous work shows that preparation must occur before death.
Creation from dust in the same surah does not clarify personal moral preparation.
Disbelief is linked to tasting punishment, a direct but limited consequence.
Righteous believing effort is neither denied nor lost, but recorded.
The God-conscious receive enduring gardens as their recompense.
The brothers plan wrongdoing while projecting later reform; the connection is only ironic.
Disbelief and obstruction of God's way cause deeds to be lost.
Praise at evening and noon does not clarify the focus relation.
Disbelief in God's signs and meeting makes deeds collapse and lose weight at judgment.
Contrasts severe punishment for disbelief with forgiveness and reward for faithful righteous work.
Same-surah resurrection confirmation is relevant context but lacks the action-to-self relation.
Same-surah faithful righteous workers are placed in joyful gardens, showing the realized outcome.
A believer who performs righteous deeds receives the highest ranks.
Bodily witnesses testify to what people acquired, making personal deeds inescapably present.
Faithful righteous action receives response and added grace, while disbelievers face severe punishment.
Righteous obedience is met with doubled reward and prepared generous provision.
Immediate prior context: human deeds produce corruption and make people taste part of their result.
Disbelief prevents acts from being accepted, connecting inner rejection to failed outward works.
Ignorant evil followed by repentance and reform receives forgiveness and mercy.
Same-surah limitation of guidance supports the distinction between responsive believers and the persistently astray.
The verse points to signs within selves but supplies no action or consequence relation.
Repair and action appear in a domestic reconciliation setting, only remotely parallel.
Righteous believing action leads to entry and exact freedom from injustice.
The marital signs passage does not clarify personal moral preparation.
Faith and righteous action erase evils and lead to enduring gardens.
Same-surah contrast between unfruitful gain and charity multiplied before God supports action's outcome.
Describes persistent disbelievers without developing their personal consequence.
Open disbelief nullifies deeds and ends in the Fire.
Same-surah call to return, reverence, prayer, and refusal of association reinforces the positive orientation.
Breaking the pledge harms one's own self, while fulfilling it receives a great reward.
Identifies Iblis as arrogant and among the disbelievers, without the focus's outcome relation.
Earth made as a resting surface with paths concretizes preparation for directed movement.
God's guidance and repair of believers' condition provides a related image of being made ready.
Joining the righteous is a broad aspiration without the focus's personal-result structure.
Believers commit selves and wealth by covenant for Paradise, a distinct future-oriented exchange.
Faith and righteous work lead to blessedness and a good return.
The bare mention of the self does not clarify the focus relation.
The command to give disbelievers respite lacks a personal consequence or preparation link.
Individual capacity and divinely observed conduct occur in a specific family-law setting.
Human behavior after relief is criticized, but it does not clarify righteous self-preparation.
The closest omitted parallel: good and evil are both explicitly done for or against one's own selves.
Whoever strives does so only for himself, directly locating the benefit of effort with its actor.
Each self earns only against itself, and no bearer carries another's burden.
Purification benefits its own self, while burdens remain personally borne.
Whoever earns a sin earns it only against himself.
Each soul has what it earned for it and what it earned against it.
Evil action is repaid to its doer, with no protector or helper apart from God.
The earth is made a mahd with paths, supplying the exact prepared-ground image absent from the candidate list.
No burdened soul bears another's burden, sharpening the focus's personal liability.
A person has only what he has striven for, directly grounding self-preparation in effort.
Each person's striving will be seen, completing the focus's forward-looking action sequence.
The striving person is then recompensed fully, supplying the realized outcome.
Whoever performs even an atom's weight of good will see it.
Whoever performs even an atom's weight of evil will see it.
Every soul receives in full what it earned, without injustice.
Every soul finds its good and evil actions made present before it.
God repays every soul for what it earned.
Every soul is repaid for what it strives for.
Every soul is paid in full for what it did, while God knows their deeds best.
Every soul is recompensed for what it earned; no injustice occurs that day.
Every person is held in pledge for what it earned.
Every soul is held in pledge for what it earned.
Affliction is tied to what people's hands earned, while divine pardon leaves much unexacted.
An evil deed has a matching recompense, while forgiveness and repair open another response.
Good deeds receive multiplied return and evil deeds only their like, without injustice.
Good earns something better, while evil receives only its like.
Whoever brings a good deed receives better than it and is secure from the day's terror.
Whoever brings an evil deed is cast into the Fire for what he used to do.
Punishment is tied to what hands sent ahead and to God's absence of injustice.
The consequence is explicitly attributed to what one's hands sent ahead.
Those who mislead carry their own burdens and additional burdens from their misguidance.
Guidance and misguidance return to the guided or astray self, and burdens are not transferred.
Disbelief leaves God independent, but return to Him brings disclosure of what people did.
Good is attributed to God while harm is attributed to what comes from one's own self.
Success belongs to the one who purifies the self.
Failure belongs to the one who corrupts the self.
Every soul will know what it sent ahead and left behind.
Every soul will know what it has brought forward.
